title: Lehmer's totient problem with fewer than sixteen prime factors
abstract_tex:
For a composite number $n$ whose totient divides $n-1$, earlier
published work required fourteen prime factors, and computational
announcements required fifteen. We prove a lower bound of sixteen,
at least $16001$ if $(n-1)/\varphi(n)\ge3$, and more than $10^8$ if
$3\mid n$, and that $n<2^{2^{k-7}}$ if $n$ has $k$ prime factors. For
the companion equation $\varphi(n)\mid n+1$ we show that the nine known
solutions are the only ones with at most eight prime factors, and that
a further solution prime to $3$ has at least sixteen. Each
statement is reduced by hand to a finite computation, which independent
programs carry out. We also give a reduction with one candidate for the
largest prime for each prefix. Lehmer's full conjecture remains open.
abstract_plain:
For a composite number n whose totient divides n-1, earlier
published work required fourteen prime factors, and computational

3| n, and that n<2^{2^{k-7}} if n has k prime factors. For
the companion equation phi(n)| n+1 we show that the nine known
solutions are the only ones with at most eight prime factors, and that
a further solution prime to 3 has at least sixteen. Each
statement is reduced by hand to a finite computation, which independent
programs carry out. We also give a reduction with one candidate for the
largest prime for each prefix. Lehmer's full conjecture remains open.
